title: Metabolic acidosis: renal glutamine metabolism (ammoniagenesis) maximizes acid excretion
vignette: A 68-year-old man comes to the emergency department due to abdominal pain and nausea for the past 2 days. He has a history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and underwent coronary artery bypass surgery 2 years ago. Blood pressure is 105/65 mm Hg and heart rate is 120/min and irregular. Abdominal examination reveals mild diffuse tenderness and decreased bowel sounds. Laboratory studies show sodium 142 mEq/L, chloride 104 mEq/L, bicarbonate 12 mEq/L, and creatinine 0.8 mg/dL; arterial blood gas shows pH 7.25 and PaCO2 29 mm Hg; venous lactic acid is 5.6 mmol/L (normal 0.5-2.0). ECG shows absent P waves and an irregular rate and rhythm. CT scan of the abdomen reveals colonic wall thickening with no enhancement on intravenous contrast. Urinalysis shows acidic urine. Renal metabolism of which of the following amino acids is most important for maximizing acid excretion in this patient?

clues.note: Low bicarbonate (12) with pH 7.25 = metabolic acidosis (here an anion-gap lactic acidosis).
Elevated lactate confirms an anion-gap metabolic (lactic) acidosis, which stimulates the kidney to maximize acid excretion.

clues.text: absent P waves and an irregular rate and rhythm
clues.note: Atrial fibrillation (absent P waves, irregularly irregular) is a source of embolism - here to the mesenteric circulation, causing ischemic colitis.

clues.text: colonic wall thickening with no enhancement
clues.note: Nonenhancing thickened colon = ischemic bowel; ischemic tissue undergoes anaerobic metabolism, producing lactic acid.

whatMatters: Ischemic colitis (atrial-fibrillation embolism) -> lactic (anion-gap metabolic) acidosis. The kidney maximizes acid excretion mainly by increasing AMMONIAGENESIS: renal tubular cells metabolize the amino acid GLUTAMINE to generate ammonium (NH4+, excreted with acid) and bicarbonate (reabsorbed to buffer blood). Answer D (glutamine).
strategy: Recall that in chronic/ongoing metabolic acidosis, the RENAL response that most increases net acid excretion is AMMONIAGENESIS from GLUTAMINE (yielding NH4+ excreted in urine + new bicarbonate). Pick glutamine. Reject alanine and aspartate (gluconeogenic amino acids), arginine (urea cycle - disposes of ammonia as urea, not acid excretion), and histidine (-> histamine).

eliminations.label: Alanine - gluconeogenic amino acid
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a glucogenic amino acid metabolized (in the liver) to pyruvate for gluconeogenesis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not the substrate the kidney uses to generate ammonium for acid excretion. ✅ Correct if: asking about gluconeogenesis (glucose-alanine cycle).

eliminations.label: Arginine - urea cycle (disposes ammonia as urea)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a urea cycle intermediate; hepatic metabolism yields urea + ornithine to remove ammonia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the urea cycle DISPOSES of ammonia (as urea) rather than excreting it as urinary ammonium to carry acid. ✅ Correct if: asking about ammonia detoxification via the urea cycle.

eliminations.label: Aspartate - gluconeogenic (oxaloacetate)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a glucogenic amino acid readily interconverted with oxaloacetate. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: not the renal ammoniagenesis substrate for acid excretion. ✅ Correct if: a gluconeogenesis/transamination question.

eliminations.label: Histidine - source of histamine
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an essential amino acid converted to histamine by histidine decarboxylase. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it functions in inflammation/gastric acid secretion, unrelated to renal acid excretion. ✅ Correct if: a histamine/inflammation question.

reasoning: Atrial-fibrillation embolism -> ischemic colitis -> anaerobic metabolism -> lactic (anion-gap metabolic) acidosis
The kidney maximizes acid excretion primarily by increasing ammoniagenesis
Renal tubular cells metabolize GLUTAMINE to generate ammonium (excreted with acid) + bicarbonate (reabsorbed)
mechanism: This patient has acute mesenteric/colonic ISCHEMIA from an embolus (atrial fibrillation), producing anaerobic metabolism and a LACTIC (high anion-gap metabolic) ACIDOSIS. The kidney defends pH by excreting acid in two forms: titratable acid (mainly phosphate) and - most importantly during acidosis - AMMONIUM. In renal proximal tubular cells, the amino acid GLUTAMINE is metabolized (glutaminase -> glutamate -> alpha-ketoglutarate) to generate AMMONIUM (NH4+), which is secreted into the tubular fluid and excreted in the urine (as NH4+, buffering/carrying away H+), while the same reactions generate BICARBONATE that is reabsorbed into the blood to replenish buffer. This renal AMMONIAGENESIS is upregulated in chronic/ongoing acidosis and accounts for the great majority of the increase in net acid excretion - far more than titratable acid, whose supply (phosphate) is limited. Therefore glutamine metabolism is most important for maximizing acid excretion. The distractors are gluconeogenic amino acids (alanine, aspartate), the urea-cycle amino acid (arginine, which disposes of ammonia as urea rather than excreting it), and histidine (a histamine precursor).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Renal/Biochem > renal ammoniagenesis: glutamine -> NH4+ (excreted, carries acid) + new bicarbonate (reabsorbed); upregulated in metabolic acidosis; main mechanism of increased net acid excretion.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: In metabolic acidosis, the kidney maximizes acid excretion via ammonium made from glutamine.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on ammoniagenesis, glutamine/glutaminase, titratable acid vs ammonium, anion gap, or net acid excretion? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Alanine/aspartate = gluconeogenic; arginine = urea cycle (dispose ammonia as urea); histidine = histamine - not renal acid excretion.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: metabolic acidosis -> renal glutamine metabolism -> ammonium excretion + new bicarbonate; primary route of increased acid excretion.

keywords.front: Amino acid used by kidney to maximize acid excretion
Two forms of renal acid excretion

firstAid.detail: Renal: glutamine -> NH4+ (excreted) + new HCO3- (reabsorbed); maximizes acid excretion.
GI > AF embolism -> lactic acidosis; nonenhancing thickened colon.

memoryHook: To dump acid, the kidney burns glutamine into ammonium (the urinary acid shuttle) and pockets fresh bicarbonate - glutamine is the acid-excretion workhorse in acidosis.
